messages:
maya: FYI - started getting mTLS 'unknown authority' errors from service-mesh when eu-edge talked to model-serving this morning. Looks regional (eu-west) only. Anyone triaging?
rachel: Yes. Error excerpt from envoy: `tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate (x509: certificate signed by unknown authority)` — but the presented cert chain on the ClientHello shows a CA we don't trust.
ops-oncall: I pulled IAM logs. There's a cluster of ACME signer denies around 07:12:05 for principal=svc-acme-provisioner@infra. Example: `ACME: SignCSR Deny principal=svc-acme-provisioner@infra reason=iam.policy.denied`. Also saw a KMS CreateKey denied for ca-rotation key at 07:12:02.
luis: That suggests the CA rotation job started but the provisioner couldn't sign new leaf certs because its role was revoked. The edge proxies then reloaded and ended up with a chain signed by a freshly-created intermediate CA that isn't in downstream truststores.
maya: How did proxies get a new chain if the ACME signer was denied?
rachel: Two things: (1) some regional edge nodes use a local minimal CA bundle that falls back to a cached intermediate when ACME fails; (2) the rotation job created a new intermediate CA in the keystore but the trust-distribution job that updates service truststores failed due to a config drift (missing role for trust-sync). So edge served chain containing the new intermediate but backends didn't trust it.
ops-oncall: Packet capture from a failing flow shows full chain: leaf -> intermediate-v2 -> root. Backends only trust intermediate-v1 -> root. Client certs are fine, but verification fails.
security-bot: Alert: RBAC change PR #5888 removed `acme.signer` from the `infra-deploy` group in eu-west. Related denies: 14 ACME SignCSR denies between 07:12:00-07:13:30.
luis: Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous RBAC cleanup removed both `acme.signer` and `trust-sync` roles from different service accounts used by provisioner and trust-distributor. The CA rotation job continued (created intermediate), proxies picked it up from local keystore, but trust-sync could not distribute the new intermediate to consumers due to its role being revoked. Result: trust anchor drift across regions.
maya: Immediate mitigation options?
rachel: Short-term: revert RBAC change for `acme.signer` and `trust-sync` in eu-west to restore signing and distribution. Roll back the intermediate in the keystore (revert to v1) and re-run trust-sync. Also put an emergency accept-list that allows intermediate-v2 temporarily.
ops-oncall: Rolling revert PR now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/8001  reverting role removals for acme.signer and trust-sync in eu-west. Also disabled scheduled CA rotation until we verify distribution.
luis: Post-recovery actions: 1) Add a gating check to RBAC merges that touch acme/trust-sync roles: CI must run a staging end-to-end that exercises sign + trust distribution across regions. 2) Emit IAM deny payloads to BigQuery (principal + request body) to map denies to PRs quickly. 3) Add truststore version metrics per-region and an alert if downstream truststore version != keystore intermediate version for >1 min.
maya: Also add a preflight for CA rotations: write intermediate to a staging keystore, run trust-sync smoke test to verify distribution to consumers in all regions, then atomically flip the live intermediate. No role revokes during the flip window.
ops-oncall: Added runbook note: `truststore-drift-check` steps: capture chain from client hello, compare intermediate fingerprint to keystore latest, check IAM denies for provisioner/trust-sync principals, revert roles if necessary.
security-bot: Suggested guardrails updated: block merging RBAC PRs that remove `acme.signer` or `trust-sync` without an explicit `trust-distribution-approved` tag.
rachel: After revert, I re-triggered trust-sync and backends accepted intermediate-v2. Error rate back to baseline. Will include details in the postmortem.
luis: Long-term: make ACME provisioner operations auditable with per-CSR request IDs, have trust-sync ack receipts from a quorum of regions before promoting an intermediate, and add a canary propagation delay where proxies prefer previous intermediate until N regions confirm receipt.
maya: Assignments: maya -> own postmortem + timeline; rachel -> verify trust-sync smoke test + add truststore metrics; luis -> BigQuery IAM export + RFC for gating; ops-oncall -> update runbook and CI gate.
maya: Thanks team. This is a different mode of failure than keystore decrypt denies, but still RBAC+distribution ordering causing trust anchor drift. Saving thread for RCA. :white_check_mark:
